theme: 3 terms on methods: functions that belong to a type

terms.definition: A function that lives inside a type and works with that type's data.
terms.example: Add a method to `Counter`, so it can show its own count.

terms.definition: A method on a struct that is allowed to change the struct's own properties.
terms.example: Mark it as a mutating method, so `add` can change `count`.

terms.definition: A method that you call on the type itself, not on one value of it.
terms.example: Make it a type method, so you call `Math.double(4)` without a value.

video.description:
Learn to talk about Swift methods: Method, Mutating Method and Type Method, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Method - A function that lives inside a type and works with that type's data.
Mutating Method - A method on a struct that is allowed to change the struct's own properties.
Type Method - A method that you call on the type itself, not on one value of it.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Explain Method, Mutating Method and Type Method in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.

한국어: 스위프트 타입 안에 있는 함수로, 그 타입의 데이터를 사용하는 메서드

dialogue.title: The Score methods

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I added a method to `Score`, so it can show the points.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nice. A method is just a function inside a type.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Now I want `add` to change `points`, but Swift shows an error.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Make it a mutating method. A struct needs `mutating` to change itself.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Oh, I forgot. So a mutating method can change `points`?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes, but only on a `var`, not on a `let`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Fine. Now I need the best score for every player.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then use a type method. You call `Score.best()` on the type.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: But I can call `add` on a value, right? Why not `best` too?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No. A type method belongs to the type, not to one value.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Got it. A method is for a value, a type method is for the type.
